applies_why: The judge text makes the absence of a verse naming the bodily channel a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is what the rule governs.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: “does not state a link or its contrary” — one reading forbids using a single verse's silence to stay open; the other would allow treating omitted wording as sufficient for UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is that Acts 2:30 does not name whose body is the channel, which is precisely a single verse's non-statement of the point.
